receipts.first_text_witness: Last year, this country minted about 1,200 new millionaires a day, every day, weekends included. And across roughly that same stretch, the wealth of the median American adult fell by about a fifth. Both of those things are true. Both of them came out of the same report. So, somewhere out there is a scoreboard showing the biggest numbers in recorded history hanging over a stadium that keeps getting emptier. Before you ask whether you're on track, you should probably ask which clock is timing you because there are two of them running in your life right now and you have only ever been shown one. Three people today. An electrician who's tired, a dental hygienist who turned down a wedding, and a software developer who makes more than double the electrician and can't tell you where any of it went. One retires with the most, one retires with the least. and the order will irritate you because it has almost nothing to do with what any of them earned. My name is Nick and I have spent an unreasonable share of my adult life staring at net worth percentile tables the way other people stare at fantasy football standings. If you've ever read a headline about record wealth, looked at your own account, and felt like you were reading a dispatch from a foreign country, hit subscribe and leave a like because today we're going to work out what ontrack actually means in 2026 and whether that track goes anywhere near where you've been told it goes.
receipts.last_text_witness: reads, "How many months could you stop right now today before something breaks?" For most people, that number is under one. Getting it to three will change your life more than getting it to two million ever will. And unlike 2 million, you can start on it this month. So don't ask whether you're a millionaire yet. Ask which clock is winning and then go make it the other one.
